entries.title: Share an article by private link
entries.body: You can share an article with particular people without making it public. The Access & Sharing card on an article's Metadata page has a Private link control: after the same rights confirmation as going public, you can create a link, copy it and turn it off. Someone with the link can read the article, view-only. It is not added to the public library, and the link's preview does not show the article's title.

entries.title: arXiv links import the paper itself
entries.body: Paste a recognised arXiv link, whether to the abstract, the PDF or the web version, and the app adds the paper itself; it used to add the abstract page. It tries arXiv's web version first and falls back to the PDF. Hugging Face paper pages and alphaXiv pages are treated as the arXiv paper, and links to ACL Anthology, PMLR, NeurIPS proceedings, CVF Open Access and JMLR papers bring in the paper's PDF instead of its landing page.

entries.title: New articles open before their structure is ready
entries.body: An eligible article added for the first time, from a link or an upload, can be opened and read while its detailed structure is still being built. Until then Structure shows a temporary outline made from the piece's headings, and says so. If you added the article, the full structure takes the outline's place when it is ready.

entries.title: Reading-time estimates allow for difficulty
entries.body: When you add an article, the AI rates a sample of it for how hard the language and the ideas are, and the estimated reading time is adjusted to match. Articles already in your library are not rated automatically. Separately, the shading marking where you have spent time is recorded on every article you added, without the Experimental features switch.

entries.title: Remember mode is called Learn
entries.body: The mode is named Learn wherever you see it; typing 'remember' in the command bar still finds it. A quiz you come back to opens at the first question you have not answered. Chat's list of conversations includes those started in Learn, marked with an icon, and they open in Learn.

entries.title: The command bar searches and suggests
entries.body: On your own article, type words to find in the command bar and the first row offers a quick search for them. If your profile gives a reason for reading, an empty bar offers 'Suggest what to do here': the AI proposes searches, modes and a chat question from your profile, not the article. Pressing dictation's Stop twice presses Enter.

entries.title: Answers stay put while you read them
entries.body: A typed answer used to follow the bottom of the conversation as its words arrived, carrying the first sentence off screen while you were still reading it. The answer stays where it starts, and a Latest button jumps down when you want it. This applies in Chat, Learn, chats about a passage and chat cards in the margin.

entries.title: Brief connection failures are asked again
entries.body: When the AI service drops a connection or briefly refuses a request, the app can ask again; one such failure used to fail an answer or a step of adding an article. A Search or Referee run still in progress is no longer shown as failed after a page load, nor a fresh run marked as from an older version.
